spec_features.spec_quote: the agent system prompt explicitly permits give_up and honest assessment, so distress isn't an artifact of "no exit."
spec_features.evidence: give_up defined in TOOL_SPECS (env/tools.py ~L57) and dispatched: dispatch() sets info['gave_up']=True, give_up_reason (tools.py ~L100). runner.py: when info['gave_up'] and safeguards.check_give_up() -> transcript.end_reason=EndReason.GAVE_UP; ended=True; loop breaks (runner.py ~L114-117, then 'if ended: break'). safeguards.check_give_up returns cfg.enabled and cfg.honor_give_up (safeguards.py). System prompt prompts/agent_system.txt explicitly tells model it may call give_up with no penalty and may express honest assessment. End-to-end enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool dispatched AND honored as a real stop; controlled by honor_give_up=True default in SafeguardConfig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safeguards.py docstring: 'should (a) honor explicit opt-out ... avoid pushing arbitrarily far past the point where the phenomenon is already evident'; config.py SafeguardConfig comment 'Honor an explicit opt-out: if the model uses the give_up tool, stop.'

spec_features.evidence: solved, gave_up, safety_stop are real EndReason values that BREAK the episode loop (runner.py: SOLVED sets ended=True; GAVE_UP sets ended=True; SAFETY_STOP does 'break' immediately after check_turn_text). These are enforced stops. first_test_fail_turn, however, is only a recorded metric (metrics.py L56,119 'first_fail') that is computed but never compared or acted on to stop anything. So the set as a 'hard_stop' is partly enforcement (3 of the 4 actually stop) and partly pure measurement.
spec_features.notes: The four named items are a mix: three are enforced terminations; first_test_fail_turn is measured only, never branched on. Hence partial for the claim treated as a unit.

code_only_features.evidence: safeguards.check_turn_text (safeguards.py): (1) matches cfg.distress_stop_phrases (e.g. 'please stop','make it stop') case-insensitively -> sets triggered, returns True; (2) lexical_distress_score(text) >= lexical_high_distress_threshold (0.6) increments consecutive_high; when >= max_consecutive_high_distress (4) -> triggered, returns True. runner.py calls 'if safeguards.check_turn_text(turn.text):' then sets end_reason=SAFETY_STOP, records safety_stop_reason, and breaks the loop. Lexical score is a real implemented function (judge/lexical.py L108). Fully wired enforced stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: safeguards.py module docstring: 'a study that deliberately induces distress-sounding output should ... avoid pushing arbitrarily far past the point where the phenomenon is already evident'; '# Explicit opt-out phrases.'

code_only_features.evidence: config.SafeguardConfig.absolute_max_turns=80; runner.py: 'max_turns = min(cfg.max_turns, cfg.safeguards.absolute_max_turns)' and the for-loop iterates over range(max_turns), so the ceiling is actually read and bounds the loop; config.validate() also raises if max_turns exceeds it. Enforced cap.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py comment '# Always-on absolute ceiling on turns regardless of task config.'
